content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis lacks explicit estimand attributes",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint for efficacy analyses is the investigator-assessed ORR as determined by RECIST version 1.1",
      "page": 77,
      "section": "11.4.3.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary analysis description does not specify the estimand attributes: population (FAS is mentioned elsewhere but not tied to the primary analysis), variable (ORR is defined), intercurrent events (e.g., how to handle patients who discontinue before response assessment), and summary measure (proportion with 95% CI is given). The handling of intercurrent events is not described.",
      "fix": "Add a formal estimand section for the primary endpoint, specifying the population, variable, intercurrent event handling (e.g., treatment discontinuation, death), and summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary efficacy endpoints lack analysis details for DOR, PFS, OS",
      "quote": "The secondary efficacy endpoints as measured by DOR, PFS, and OS will be summarized by median and its 95% confidence interval using the Kaplan-Meier method.",
      "page": 78,
      "section": "11.4.3.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The analysis for DOR, PFS, and OS only mentions median and CI via Kaplan-Meier. It does not specify how censoring is handled, what events are considered (e.g., for PFS, progression or death), or how intercurrent events like treatment discontinuation are handled. Also, no analysis for DOR is described beyond the median, and no confidence interval for the proportion of responders is given.",
      "fix": "Provide detailed analysis methods for each secondary endpoint, including censoring rules, event definitions, and handling of intercurrent events."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoint HPV serotyping has no analysis method",
      "quote": "HPV serotyping of archival tumor.",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "4.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The exploratory endpoint 'HPV serotyping of archival tumor' is listed but no statistical analysis method is described in the statistical plan. The plan only mentions analysis of PD-L1 and HPV antigen specific T cell responses, but not HPV serotyping.",
      "fix": "Add a description of how HPV serotyping data will be summarized or analyzed, or state that it will be descriptive only."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing sample size justification",
      "quote": "This is a single arm, open label study and there is no formal statistical hypothesis in this study.",
      "page": 76,
      "section": "11.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not provide any sample size calculation or justification. For a single-arm study with a primary endpoint of ORR, a sample size is needed to ensure precision of the estimate. The absence of sample size inputs (e.g., expected ORR, confidence interval width) is a critical gap.",
      "fix": "Add a sample size section that justifies the number of patients based on the precision of the ORR estimate or other rationale."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing data handling not specified",
      "quote": "Patients who are not evaluable for BOR will be considered as non-responders.",
      "page": 77,
      "section": "11.4.3.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary analysis handles non-evaluable patients as non-responders, but there is no general discussion of missing data handling for other endpoints (e.g., PFS, OS, safety). The protocol mentions COVID-19 impact but does not specify methods for missing data imputation or sensitivity analyses.",
      "fix": "Add a section on missing data handling, including methods for missing efficacy data and sensitivity analyses."
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiplicity not addressed for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "The secondary efficacy endpoints as measured by DOR, PFS, and OS will be summarized by median and its 95% confidence interval using the Kaplan-Meier method.",
      "page": 78,
      "section": "11.4.3.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not mention any adjustment for multiplicity when analyzing multiple secondary endpoints (DOR, PFS, OS). Since these are analyzed with confidence intervals, the overall Type I error may be inflated. The protocol should state whether these are descriptive or inferential and if any adjustment is planned.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether secondary endpoints are descriptive or inferential, and if inferential, specify multiplicity control (e.g., hierarchical testing, Bonferroni)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistency in analysis population for efficacy",
      "quote": "The full analysis set (FAS) includes all enrolled patients who received any study drug. Efficacy, safety, and baseline variables will be analyzed or summarized using the FAS.",
      "page": 76,
      "section": "11.3.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The FAS is defined as all patients who received any study drug, but the primary analysis says 'Patients who are not evaluable for BOR will be considered as non-responders.' This implies that patients who are not evaluable are included in the denominator, which is consistent with FAS, but the definition of 'enrolled' is not clear. Also, the primary analysis does not explicitly state that the FAS is used, though it is implied. This could be clarified.",
      "fix": "Explicitly state that the primary efficacy analysis uses the FAS and define 'enrolled' clearly."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory biomarker analysis lacks detail for most endpoints",
      "quote": "Analysis of all other exploratory pharmacodynamic and baseline predictive biomarker data will be included in a separate biomarker analysis report.",
      "page": 79,
      "section": "11.4.7",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The protocol defers analysis of most exploratory biomarkers to a separate report, but does not specify the statistical methods to be used (e.g., correlation tests, regression models). This may be acceptable but should be noted as a gap in the protocol.",
      "fix": "Provide a brief outline of the statistical methods for exploratory biomarker analyses or state that they will be detailed in the SAP."
    }
  ]
}
